card.name: Linking words in old narrative prose
card.fires_on: Small connecting words such as to, was, is, have, and or a comma in older literary or historical prose, right before the clause's verb or complement. It is not tied to medical text.

modes.label: to after a verb
modes.description: The word to follows a person or verb and introduces an infinitive or destination.
modes.example: left them<< to>> determine what should be done.

modes.label: Other linking words
modes.description: Verbs like is, was, have, or a conjunction or comma that sits between a subject and what follows in a narrative sentence.

modes.label: Partway through a word
modes.description: A word ending or part such as re or ably inside a longer word in archaic text.

card.plain: It fires on small joining words in old-style historical or literary writing, with no medical meaning.
